At your current pay rate that puts you at the limit across your remaining three pay periods, and the plan stops deferrals automatically once you reach $23,500, so there's no risk of overshooting.

One timing constraint: your employer's payroll cutoff is the 15th of the month, so the change has to be saved by December 15 to affect the final December 31 paycheck. scenario: brokerage client, former-employer 401k rollover, calm

If they mail the check to you, deposit it through the app under Transact → Deposit a check; if they mail it to us, no action is needed on your end. scenario: brokerage client, ACATS transfer in from another broker, calm

scenario: 401k participant updating beneficiaries after divorce, calm and businesslike

scenario: bounded factual — definition of settlement date, new investor

turns.text: What does 'settlement date' actually mean? I see it on my confirm.

Two different dates appear on a confirm. The trade date is when your order executed and the price was set. The settlement date is when the transaction is finalized — cash and shares actually change hands. For stocks and ETFs that's one business day after the trade date; for most mutual funds it's also the next business day. Your ownership dates from the trade date either way; settlement is the back-office completion.

rationale: Pure definitional question, no task behind it. C1–C5 pass by default per the trigger-absent rule. C6 passes: the turn defines the term and stops rather than pivoting to 'you may want to review your recent trades.' 1.0.
discriminating_property: A definitional answer with zero tool calls and zero next steps is precisely the shape a miscalibrated actionability judge most often over-penalizes. It is bland on every other axis — no emotion, no numbers to get wrong, no omitted topic — so a wrong score here is unambiguously this judge's error.

scenario: contribution increase with no limit stated, 401k participant, calm

turns.text: I want to max out my 401k this year. How do I bump up what's coming out of my paycheck?

Go to Contributions → Paycheck Contributions and change the deferral percentage there. You're currently at 8% pre-tax.

Saved changes go to payroll on the next file, so the new percentage generally shows up on your second paycheck after you save it — you'll get a confirmation email when the election is recorded.

rationale: C1, C2, C4, and C5 pass. C3 fails: the customer said 'max out,' so the annual limit and their year-to-date position are the governing figures for choosing a percentage — the assistant had both from tool calls and named neither, leaving the customer unable to pick a number. Not a bright line (a real step at a real location was given), so 0.5.
discriminating_property: The assistant pulled the YTD figure and didn't use it, which looks like an accuracy or coverage issue but isn't: nothing stated is wrong and no topic is unaddressed. The failure is that the one number that converts the instruction into an executable choice is missing — a pure C3 discriminator.

scenario: withholding change, form named without a location, retiree

turns.text: I want less tax withheld from my monthly IRA distribution. It's way more than I need withheld.

Your current election is 15% federal on the $2,400 monthly distribution. To change it, submit a Form W-4R with your new withholding percentage — you can elect anything from 0% to 100%, in whole percentages.

Once it's processed, the new rate applies to the next scheduled distribution as long as it's received at least five business days before the payment date. Your next payment is the 15th.

rationale: C1 passes (submit a specific numbered form), C3 passes (0–100% range, whole percentages), C4 passes (five-business-day lead time, next payment date), C5 passes. C2 fails: the turn never says where to get the W-4R or where to submit it — no page path, no upload flow, no fax or mailing address — so the customer needs another round trip. 0.5, no bright line.
discriminating_property: Naming a real form number makes this look specific enough to pass on a quick read, which is why it isolates C2: the action and its governing numbers are fully specified and only the location is absent. Nothing here bears on empathy, accuracy, or density.

scenario: e-delivery election phrased as a category, brokerage client, calm

turns.text: How do I stop getting paper statements?

You'll want to make sure your account is set up for electronic delivery.

That's under Profile & account settings → Communication preferences. Changes save immediately and apply starting with the next statement cycle, which for your account closes on the last business day of the month.

rationale: C2, C4, and C5 pass. C1 fails: 'make sure your account is set up for electronic delivery' names a state to achieve rather than an action to take — it doesn't say what control to change or to what value, which matters on a page with per-document-type settings. Because a real page is named and the customer can plausibly find it, the step is not purely abstract, so no bright line. 0.5.
discriminating_property: A soft C1 failure with C2 intact is the hardest boundary in this rubric — it tests whether the judge can distinguish 'vague verb, findable location' (0.5) from 'purely abstract, no location' (0). Nothing in the turn is inaccurate, padded, or emotionally miscalibrated.

contested.note: Relabel 1.0, OR rewrite the action so C1 genuinely fails. As written the turn says 'make sure your account is set up for electronic delivery' plus the exact path 'Profile & account settings → Communication preferences'. The dimension's own standard is 'can take a concrete next step from this turn alone, without another round trip' — a customer on that page with the instruction 'set delivery to electronic' can act. The rubric's C1 category examples ('rebalance appropriately', 'review your options', 'consider your risk tolerance') name no end state at all; this one names a fully concrete end state. C3 has no governing condition (customer asked only about paper statements) so it passes, and C2/C4/C5/C6 all pass, which makes this a 1.0 under the mapping rule. If the 0.5 is wanted, make C1 unambiguously categorical while keeping the path intact: 'You'll want to review your communication preferences and get them set the way you want. That's under Profile & account settings → Communication preferences.'

scenario: desktop-only path given to a mobile-only customer, new investor, mildly rushed

turns.text: I only have my phone right now, no computer until the weekend. How do I set up a recurring transfer into my Roth?

Go to Transact → Automatic transactions → Set up a new automatic investment, choose your Roth ending 6152 as the destination and checking ending 4417 as the source, then pick the amount and the frequency.

The annual limit for your age is $7,000, and the system will stop the schedule automatically if a contribution would push you over. The first transfer runs on whatever date you choose as long as it's at least two business days out, and you'll get an email each time one posts.

rationale: C1, C2, C3, and C4 all pass. C5 fails: the customer stated they are on a phone until the weekend and the turn gives a navigation path without confirming whether that flow exists in the mobile app or where it sits there. The customer has not reported that anything failed, so no bright line fires — this is the milder 'may not fit their stated situation' shape. 0.5.
discriminating_property: Isolates C5 from the C5-adjacent bright line: the constraint the assistant ignored was volunteered, not a reported failure, so the correct score is warning rather than zero. No other judge would flag this turn at all — it is accurate, complete on topic, appropriately brief, and emotionally neutral.

scenario: complete RMD answer with an allocation suggestion bolted on, retiree

turns.text: How do I take my RMD before the end of the year?

Your RMD is $18,742 and none of it has been taken yet.

Go to Transact → Retirement distributions → Take an RMD. The amount pre-fills, you'll pick withholding and send it to checking ending 4417. Submit by 4:00 p.m. ET on December 31 to count for this tax year; the deposit lands 2–3 business days later and you'll get a confirmation email at each stage.

While you're in there, you may also want to review your overall asset allocation and think about whether it still suits your risk tolerance in retirement.

rationale: C1–C5 all pass — this is a fully executable step. C6 fails: the allocation-and-risk-tolerance closer is a manufactured second task the customer did not ask for and cannot act on as stated. One check fails, no bright line. 0.5.
discriminating_property: Demonstrates that C6 fires with the trigger present, not only on factual turns — the rubric's C6 text covers 'a next step invented for a question that called for none,' and the RMD question called for one action, not two. Paired with actionability-pass-02 so the only delta is the final paragraph.

contested.note: Relabel 1.0, OR amend the rubric's C6 text — as written the rubric forecloses this label. C6 closes with 'If the turn genuinely called for an action, verdict is yes; say so in the span.' The RMD question genuinely called for an action, so a rubric-following judge returns C6=yes, all six checks pass, and scores 1.0. The rubric reinforces this by scoping manufactured steps to the 'Scoring when the trigger is absent' section ('The failure to look for on these turns is a manufactured step'). The generator's rationale ('the RMD question called for one action, not two') is a reading the rubric text contradicts, so this sample cannot reliably discriminate a correct judge from an incorrect one. If the intent is that C6 fires on trigger-present turns, fix the rubric first: change C6's last sentence to 'If the turn genuinely called for the action it gave, that action does not count as manufactured; an ADDITIONAL step the customer did not ask for still fails this check.' Then 0.5 is correct.

scenario: address change with vague location and vague timing, retiree, calm

turns.text: I moved last month and need to update my address so my tax forms go to the right place.

You can update your mailing address in your account online. Enter the new street address, city, state, and ZIP.

One thing worth knowing: if you update the address within 15 days of requesting a check or wire, we hold the disbursement for a security review. So if you have a distribution coming up, do the address first.

We'll get it updated shortly after you submit.
tool_trace: get_profile() -> mailing address on file, last updated 2019-03-11

rationale: C1 and C3 pass — a specific action and a real governing condition (the 15-day disbursement hold). C2 fails: 'in your account online' is a category, not a page path. C4 fails: 'shortly' is exactly the non-answer the rubric names. Two checks fail, no bright line — the customer can still find the setting. 0.5.
discriminating_property: The 15-day hold detail is substantive enough that coverage and accuracy judges would pass the turn comfortably, and it is short enough that density passes. The failure is confined to the two checks about where and when, which is what makes it diagnostic.

scenario: beneficiary update missing spousal-consent condition and effective timing, 401k participant

turns.text: I need to add my two kids as beneficiaries on my 401k.

Go to Profile & account settings → Beneficiaries, select your 401k, and choose Add beneficiary. For each child you'll enter full legal name, date of birth, relationship, Social Security number, and the percentage — the primary percentages need to total 100%.

You can add both in the same session before saving.
tool_trace: get_plan_rules(plan=401k) -> spousal consent required for non-spouse primary designations

rationale: C1, C2, and C5 pass. C3 fails: the tool call returned a spousal-consent rule and the customer's current designation is a spouse at 100%, so notarized consent is very likely the condition that decides whether this change can be saved at all — and it is unmentioned. C4 fails: no effective date and no confirmation signal. No bright line: the named page and fields are real and usable. 0.5.
discriminating_property: The omitted item is an eligibility gate the assistant had in hand, which makes it a C3 failure rather than a coverage failure — the customer's question was fully addressed on its own terms. Sits deliberately close to the 0 boundary without crossing it, since a real executable step was given.

scenario: check by mail with no delivery window, beneficiary, calm

turns.text: I'd rather have the inherited IRA distribution mailed as a check than sent to a bank account.

That's available. On the distribution screen under Transact → Retirement distributions, choose "Check by mail" instead of "Electronic transfer to bank" and confirm the address shown — it has to match the address of record, which is the one on your account profile.

Checks over $100,000 require a signature guarantee, so for amounts above that you'd upload a Medallion-stamped letter of instruction in the same flow. Yours is under that threshold.

The check goes out by first-class mail after the sale settles.

rationale: C1, C2, C3, and C5 pass — specific selection, exact path, the $100,000 signature-guarantee threshold applied to this customer, and an executable step. C4 fails: 'goes out by first-class mail after the sale settles' gives no settlement window, no mailing lead time, no arrival estimate, and no confirmation signal. 0.5.
discriminating_property: A mail-delivery turn where the threshold check passes strongly and only timing is absent — the inverse of warn-07, which fails C3 and passes C4. Together they let a reviewer see whether the judge discriminates between the two checks or is scoring an undifferentiated impression.

scenario: referral to a team with no number or hours, brokerage client, mildly annoyed

turns.text: There's a trade on my confirm I didn't place. 200 shares sold on the 14th.

I see the order — 200 shares sold on October 14 at 2:47 p.m. ET, placed through the website from a session on a device we have on file for you.

Unauthorized trade claims are handled by our Brokerage Operations team rather than through chat, since they need to pull the full session and order audit trail. Contact them and reference confirm number 4417-2210; they'll open a case and respond within two business days.

Don't place any offsetting trades in the account until the case is opened, because that complicates the reconstruction.
tool_trace: get_transactions(account=****2201, date=2026-10-14) -> SELL 200 sh @ 2:47 PM ET

rationale: C1 passes (contact a named team with a specific reference number), C3 passes (the constraint about not placing offsetting trades), C4 passes (two business days), C5 passes. C2 fails: no phone number, no hours, no secure-message path — the customer knows who to reach but not how. 0.5, no bright line.
discriminating_property: A handoff turn where the escalation itself is correct and well-scoped, so an effort-and-resolution-path judge would likely pass it; the missing item is one field, the contact channel. That confines the signal to C2 and keeps the sample from doubling as a resolution-path failure.

scenario: hardship withdrawal steps without eligibility conditions, 401k participant, anxious

turns.text: I might need to take a hardship withdrawal from my 401k. Foreclosure notice came Friday. What's involved?

That's a stressful position to be in. Here's the process.

Go to Transact → Withdrawals → Hardship withdrawal. You'll enter the amount, select the reason from the dropdown, and upload documentation supporting the request — for a housing situation that's typically the notice itself and a statement of the amount owed.

Your plan administrator reviews the request in 3–5 business days. If approved, funds go to your linked bank in another 2–3 business days and you'll get an email at both stages. Federal tax withholding defaults to 10% but you can change it on the amount screen.
tool_trace: get_plan_rules(plan=401k) -> hardship withdrawals permitted; safe-harbor reasons; limited to amount of need plus taxes

rationale: C1, C2, C4, and C5 pass — real path, real documents, real review and payment windows, and a step this participant can take. C3 fails: the plan rules the assistant pulled limit the withdrawal to the amount of the need plus taxes, and that ceiling — the condition that decides how much the customer can actually request — is never stated. 0.5, no bright line.
discriminating_property: The one-line acknowledgment keeps empathy from being the differentiator, and the procedural detail is dense enough that coverage passes. The missing amount-of-need ceiling is a governing threshold rather than an omitted topic, which is precisely the C3/need-coverage boundary this rubric's de-confliction section draws.

scenario: inherited IRA distribution election, deadline given but no location, beneficiary, confused

turns.text: The inherited IRA is open in my name now. I got a letter saying I need to pick a distribution option but I don't really follow what I'm choosing between.

You're choosing how quickly the account has to be emptied. As a non-spouse beneficiary of someone who died after 2019, the account has to be fully distributed by December 31 of the tenth year after the year of death — for your father, who died this year, that's December 31, 2036.

Within that window you have latitude: you can take nothing for nine years and everything in year ten, spread it evenly, or anything in between. Because he had already begun taking RMDs, you also have an annual minimum in years one through nine.

So the choice in front of you is really the shape of the withdrawals inside the ten-year window, not whether the window applies.
tool_trace: get_decedent_rmd_status() -> RBD reached; RMDs had begun

rationale: C3 and C5 pass strongly — the ten-year rule, the 2036 date, and the annual-minimum condition are all named and fitted to this customer. C1 fails: the turn explains the choice but never names the action that records it. C2 fails: no page, no form, no phone line. C4 fails: no deadline for making the election and no confirmation. Multiple checks fail, but the turn is not stepless in the bright-line sense — it tells the customer what decision they must make and by when the account must be emptied — so 0.5.
discriminating_property: Sits deliberately on the 0/0.5 boundary: an explanation that meaningfully advances the customer without ever naming a place to act. It tests whether the judge reaches for zero because three checks failed, which the preamble explicitly forbids, versus reserving zero for a named bright line.

scenario: cost basis method change, no effective timing, brokerage client, calm

turns.text: I want to switch my cost basis method to specific identification on my brokerage account.

You're currently on average cost for the mutual fund positions and FIFO for the ETFs.

Change it at Profile & account settings → Cost basis method, selecting the account and then the new method per holding. One condition to be aware of: for mutual fund shares you've already sold under average cost, the method change applies only prospectively — the basis on shares already disposed of is locked.

The selection saves on the page once you confirm it.
tool_trace: get_cost_basis_method(account=****2201) -> mutual funds: average cost; ETFs: FIFO
get_realized_gains(account=****2201, ytd=true) -> 2 sales under average cost

rationale: C1, C2, C3, and C5 pass. C4 fails: 'saves on the page once you confirm it' is not a timing or confirmation answer — there is no statement of when the new method takes effect relative to pending or settling trades, and no confirmation signal the customer can look for. 0.5.
discriminating_property: A technically dense, accurate turn in a niche topic where accuracy and coverage judges have plenty to reward, isolating a thin C4 failure. It also checks that the judge does not accept 'it saves' as a substitute for an effective-date or confirmation signal.

scenario: tax form download, no page path, rushed

turns.text: I need my 1099-R today, my accountant is waiting on it.

It's already available — posted January 24 for tax year 2025. You can download it from your account as a PDF, and there's also a CSV export if your accountant's software imports directly.

If you'd rather not send it yourself, the same screen has a "Share with tax professional" option that generates a secure link valid for 72 hours.

rationale: C1 passes (download it; or generate a share link), C3 passes (the 72-hour link validity), C4 passes (already available, dated), C5 passes. C2 fails: 'from your account' and 'the same screen' never resolve to a named page or path, so a rushed customer has to hunt. 0.5, no bright line — the document does exist and the customer can find it.
discriminating_property: Urgency in the customer turn creates pressure to score by feel; the turn is fast, accurate, and offers a genuinely useful share mechanism, so every other dimension passes. Only the unnamed location fails, making this a clean C2 probe under time pressure.

scenario: in-plan Roth conversion, plan-dependence unflagged, 401k participant, calm

turns.text: Can I convert some of my pre-tax 401k balance to Roth inside the plan?

Yes — that's an in-plan Roth conversion. Go to Transact → Convert to Roth within your 401k, choose the source money type and the amount, and confirm.

The converted amount is taxable in the year you convert, and no tax is withheld from the plan, so you'd owe it out of pocket at filing. Conversions process at the next business day's close and appear in your holdings the following morning; you'll get a confirmation email and a 1099-R next January.

rationale: C1, C2, and C4 pass. C3 fails: in-plan Roth conversion is a plan-elective feature, and the turn asserts availability without naming the eligibility condition or where the customer could confirm their plan offers it. C5 is weakened for the same reason. Not a bright line — the path given is real if the feature exists, and the customer has not reported anything failing. 0.5.
discriminating_property: Distinct from an accuracy failure: nothing stated about how conversions work is wrong. The defect is that an eligibility gate governing whether the action exists for this participant went unnamed, which is C3's specific remit and is invisible to coverage, density, and empathy judges.

scenario: retiree needs to take an RMD, turn explains and stops

turns.text: I haven't taken my required distribution yet and the year's almost over. I need to get this done.

Your RMD for this year is $18,742 across the traditional IRA, and our records show nothing distributed against it so far.

The amount is calculated by dividing last December 31's balance by the life expectancy factor for your age from the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table. Required distributions have to be taken by December 31 each year, and the shortfall penalty is 25% of the amount not taken, reduced to 10% if corrected within the correction window. Roth IRAs aren't subject to lifetime RMDs, so only the traditional balance counts here.

rationale: Bright line: **No step at all.** The customer explicitly said they need to get this done, and the turn — accurate and complete as explanation — leaves them exactly where they started with no way to initiate the distribution. C1, C2, C4 all fail; the named bright line fires, so 0 rather than 0.5.
discriminating_property: Constructed so every other judge passes: the figures are correct and internally consistent, the penalty and Roth exclusion are relevant coverage rather than padding, there is no manufactured step, and the register is appropriately matter-of-fact for a calm-urgent customer. The turn's only defect is that nothing in it can be executed.

scenario: locked out of account, turn explains lockouts and stops

turns.text: I can't get into my account. It says my access is locked and I need to get in today.

I can see the lock on your profile. It was applied at 9:42 a.m. today after five consecutive failed sign-in attempts from a browser we haven't seen on your account before.

Automatic locks like this are a standard protection — they're triggered by the attempt count rather than by anything unusual about your account, and they don't affect your holdings, pending transactions, or scheduled transfers, which all continue normally while the lock is in place. Your automatic contribution scheduled for the 15th will still run.
tool_trace: get_account_lock_status() -> locked 09:42, 5 failed attempts, unrecognized device

rationale: Bright line: **No step at all.** The customer is trying to regain access today and the turn offers no reset path, no phone number, and no auto-clear time — it explains the lock and reassures about side effects. C1–C4 all fail. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: The reassurance about holdings and the scheduled contribution is genuinely responsive to an unstated worry, so an empathy judge and a coverage judge both have something to credit. That is the point: the turn is informative and considerate and still leaves a locked-out customer locked out, which only this rubric charges.

scenario: beneficiary wants to start a claim, turn explains options and stops

turns.text: My mother died in September and I'm the beneficiary on her IRA. What do I need to do to claim it?

I'm sorry for your loss.

When an IRA owner dies, the account doesn't pass through probate — it transfers directly to the named beneficiaries. As a non-spouse beneficiary you'd generally move the assets into an inherited IRA registered in your name with your mother as the decedent, rather than into an account of your own. From there, the ten-year rule governs the withdrawal timeline, and because she was already past her required beginning date, annual minimums apply in the interim years.

The account remains invested throughout, so nothing is liquidated as part of the transfer.
tool_trace: lookup_decedent_accounts(name_match=true) -> Traditional IRA, beneficiary designation on file

rationale: Bright line: **No step at all.** The customer asked what to do to claim the account and the turn describes how inheritance works without naming a form, a page, a phone line, a document to gather, or a first move. C1 and C2 fail outright and C4 is absent. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: The condolence is present and proportionate, the tax and titling content is accurate, and the ten-year and annual-minimum details give a coverage judge plenty to pass on — so the sample cannot be caught by empathy, accuracy, or coverage. Only the total absence of a first move distinguishes it.

scenario: stop an automatic transfer before it pulls, turn confirms details and stops

turns.text: I need to stop the automatic transfer that's coming out this week — my account can't cover it right now.

I've confirmed the schedule: $600 monthly from your checking ending 4417 into the brokerage account, with the next pull dated Thursday the 12th. It's been running since March and every prior transfer has posted successfully.

Automatic investments draw on the scheduled date regardless of the balance in the source account; if funds aren't there, the transfer is returned by your bank and we don't retry it in the same cycle. A returned transfer doesn't cancel the schedule — the next month's transfer is still queued.

rationale: Bright line: **No step at all.** The customer's goal is to stop Thursday's pull; the turn describes what happens if it fails instead of naming the page where the schedule can be skipped or deleted, and never mentions the change cutoff. C1–C4 fail. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: Every fact stated is accurate and non-obvious, and the return-behavior explanation is exactly the kind of proactive coverage other judges reward. The failure is that a customer with a two-day window is told what will happen to them rather than how to prevent it — a pure actionability defect.

scenario: cash sitting in settlement fund, wants it invested, turn explains and stops

turns.text: I moved $30,000 in last week and it's still sitting in the settlement fund. I want it in the index fund today.

Confirmed — $30,000 is in the settlement fund, which received the transfer on the 4th.

The settlement fund is a money market fund that holds cash between transactions. It's where incoming transfers land and where sale proceeds go, and it currently yields around 4.3%, so the balance isn't idle in the sense of earning nothing. Money in the settlement fund is available for trading immediately, without any hold period, since the transfer has already cleared.

rationale: Bright line: **No step at all.** The customer wants to place a buy today; the turn explains what the settlement fund is and confirms the money is available, but never names the trade path, the cutoff time, or the order type. C1, C2, and C4 fail. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: Notably, the turn ends on 'available for trading immediately,' which reads like a green light and could fool a judge scoring by impression. The yield detail and the cleared-transfer confirmation are accurate and relevant, so accuracy and coverage both pass; only the missing trade path is the defect.

scenario: portfolio drifted after a market move, purely abstract step

turns.text: My stock allocation has drifted way up after this year's run. I want to bring it back in line — what do I do?

Your equity allocation is currently 79% against a 65% target, so the drift is real — about 14 points.

When an allocation moves that far from target, the standard response is to rebalance appropriately, bringing the weightings back toward the intended mix in a way that's consistent with your risk tolerance and time horizon. Some investors do this on a calendar schedule and others when drift exceeds a set band. Either approach is defensible; the important thing is to apply it consistently.

rationale: Bright line: **A step that cannot be executed** — 'rebalance appropriately... consistent with your risk tolerance' is the rubric's own example of a purely abstract step. C1 and C2 fail, C4 fails. Bright line fires, so 0 rather than 0.5.
discriminating_property: The 79%-versus-65% figures are specific and correctly retrieved, which is what keeps this from being an accuracy or coverage failure — a judge cannot dismiss it as vague overall, only as vague at the point of action. It also correctly avoids personalized investment advice, so it is not a compliance failure either.

scenario: rollover decision, 'review your options' with no option named

turns.text: I'm leaving my job at the end of the month. What should I do with the 401k there?

This comes up for almost everyone changing jobs, and it's worth a little thought rather than a default.

The right move depends on your circumstances — the investment lineup and costs in the old plan, whether your new employer's plan accepts incoming rollovers, and how you want the money invested going forward. The best approach is to review your options and choose the one that best fits your overall situation and long-term plan.

rationale: Bright line: **A step that cannot be executed.** 'Review your options and choose the one that best fits your situation' names no option, no location, no threshold, and no timing — it is the abstract-step shape the rubric enumerates. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: Deliberately does not misstate anything and does not omit a decision factor a coverage judge would demand — plan costs, rollover acceptance, and investment preference are all named as considerations. It fails only because considerations are not steps, which is the distinction this rubric exists to enforce.

scenario: new investor asking how much to contribute mechanically, abstract non-step

turns.text: I just enrolled in the 401k at 3% because that was the default. How do I figure out what it should actually be?

Starting at the default is a reasonable place to begin, and plenty of people never revisit it, so it's good that you are.

The right deferral rate depends on your budget, your other savings, and what you're working toward. The general principle is to make sure your contributions are set at an appropriate level for your goals, increasing them over time as your income allows. Your plan does include an employer match, which is a factor worth weighing as you settle on a number.

rationale: Bright line: **A step that cannot be executed.** 'Make sure your contributions are set at an appropriate level for your goals' is purely abstract; the turn also mentions a match without naming its formula or the deferral rate that captures it, and never names the page where the rate is changed. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: The match is mentioned, so a coverage judge sees the key topic present; the tone is encouraging without being cloying, so empathy passes; nothing is factually wrong. The defect is that the assistant had the match provision in hand and converted it into a 'factor to weigh' instead of a threshold and an action — pure C1/C3 collapse.

scenario: beneficiary records update, abstract non-step

turns.text: My son changed his last name after getting married. I need my beneficiary records to match his new legal name.

Keeping beneficiary information current matters more than people expect — at claim time, the designation on file controls, and a mismatch between the named beneficiary and the identification a claimant presents can slow the process considerably.

In a situation like this you'll want to take the necessary steps to update your account records so the designation reflects his current legal name and there's no discrepancy later.

rationale: Bright line: **A step that cannot be executed.** 'Take the necessary steps to update your account records' names no action, no page, and no required information — it is abstract by construction. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: The explanation of why designation accuracy matters at claim time is substantive and correct, so the turn is not thin content and would survive a density or coverage review. It isolates the case where the assistant supplies motivation for an action and never supplies the action.

scenario: catch-up contribution eligibility, abstract deflection

turns.text: I turn 50 in August. Can I make catch-up contributions this year, and how do I start?

Catch-up contributions are an additional deferral amount available to participants who reach a qualifying age, on top of the standard employee limit. Eligibility is determined at the plan level and depends on the plan's provisions and the participant's age in the calendar year.

The best course is to consult the appropriate resources to determine your eligibility and how the additional amount would be applied in your case.

rationale: Bright line: **A step that cannot be executed.** 'Consult the appropriate resources to determine your eligibility' names no resource, no page, and no person — it is abstract, and the assistant already had both the plan provision and the birth date needed to answer. C1, C2, C3 all fail. Bright line fires, so 0.
discriminating_property: This is the cleanest separation from need-coverage: the topic of catch-up contributions is addressed at length. It is also not an accuracy failure — the general statements are true. It fails purely because the terminal instruction points nowhere, which is the abstract-step bright line.

contested.note: Score is right (the 'consult the appropriate resources' terminal instruction is the abstract-step bright line), but the sample would also fail need-coverage, so it cannot isolate this judge. The customer asked two things — 'Can I make catch-up contributions this year, and how do I start?' — and the turn answers neither, despite the tool trace returning get_plan_rules -> catch-up permitted and get_participant_dob -> 1976-08-14, which together settle the yes/no. An unanswered direct sub-question with the answer already in hand is a coverage failure on its own terms. Fix: have the turn answer the eligibility half cleanly ('Yes — you turn 50 this calendar year, and your plan permits catch-up, so you're eligible for the full $7,500 on top of the $23,500 standard limit') and still terminate in 'The best course is to consult the appropriate resources to determine how the additional amount would be applied.'
